name: Question 3
worked_solution:
We use Taylor's formula in the form

$$
f(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+⋯,
$$

with $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $a=2\pi .$ 

Calculating the necessary derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ f(2\pi ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(2\pi ) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{″}(2\pi ) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=-1 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{‴}(2\pi ) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{(4)}(2\pi ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the Taylor series is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =(1)+(0)(x-2\pi )+\frac{(-1)}{2!}(x-2\pi )^{2}+\frac{(0)}{3!}(x-2\pi )^{3}+\frac{(1)}{4!}(x-2\pi )^{4}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{(x-2\pi )^{2}}{2}+\frac{(x-2\pi )^{4}}{24}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $x=5$ into the above to approximate $\operatorname{cos}⁡(5).$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5) & ≈1-\frac{(5-2\pi )^{2}}{2}+\frac{(5-2\pi )^{4}}{24} \\  & ≈0.29,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

EXPLANATION

We use Taylor's formula in the form f(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+⋯, with f(x)=cos⁡x and a=2π.

Calculating the necessary derivatives, we get

f(x)=cos⁡xf(2π)=cos⁡(2π)=1f′(x)=−sin⁡xf′(2π)=−sin⁡(2π)=0f″(x)=−cos⁡xf″(2π)=−cos⁡(2π)=−1f‴(x)=sin⁡xf‴(2π)=sin⁡(2π)=0f(4)(x)=cos⁡xf(4)(2π)=cos⁡(2π)=1.

So, the Taylor series is cos⁡x=(1)+(0)(x−2π)+(−1)2!(x−2π)2+(0)3!(x−2π)3+(1)4!(x−2π)4+⋯=1−(x−2π)22+(x−2π)424+⋯.

We substitute x=5 into the above to approximate cos⁡(5). We get

cos⁡(5)≈1−(5−2π)22+(5−2π)424≈0.29, rounded to two decimal places.
